why: Recovers 22 gld-compat verdict rows that were discarded rather than superseded. MEASURED 2026-09-10: PRs #11662 and #11664 were closed unmerged at 13:22Z under the operator's 'rescue the 3, close the 9' batch decision, on the reasoning that a branch carrying 66 rows against main's 77 must be a subset. THE ROW COUNT WAS CORRECT AND WAS THE WRONG TEST — docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl is append-only PER RUN (writer scripts/research/gld_compat_extract.py:109 is a pure append with no dedup), so a later run with MORE rows can still lack a strategy an earlier run measured. Set-compared by (strategy, account_id): #11662 carried 11 ief_pullback_1d rows absent from main, #11664 carried 11 iaum_pullback_1d rows absent from main; main held only gld_pullback_1h, slv_pullback_1d and tlt_pullback_1d. #11664 was explicitly 'waved through with its sibling' and not row-count-checked at all — and it is the one that carried a full 77, so the check that was run was run on the wrong PR of the two. WHY IT IS WORTH A PR: ief_pullback_1d and iaum_pullback_1d are two of the four legs commit e88ef612a (MI-247) added to alpaca_live — a REAL-MONEY account — the same day, CLAUDE.md makes the per-account compat matrix mandatory before routing a strategy to an account, and this corpus's own done-condition is R2, 'the run is not done when it exits 0, it is done when its rows are readable on main'. Two of the five live legs had no verdict there. THE ROSTER IS NOT IN QUESTION: read off the closed branches, all four added legs verdict ROUTE on alpaca_live (survival 1.0, p_breach 0.0, size_state measured). This is an evidence-readability defect, not a routing error, and nothing here re-litigates the roster. TIER-1 AND WHY IT IS SAFE: the only data change is an append to a committed research corpus — no src/, no config/, no workflow, no order path, no live read. Two things were verified BEFORE writing rather than asserted after: every one of the 220 lines across both branches and main round-trips byte-identically through the writer's own json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True), so this reproduces exactly what the landing PR would have produced; and the append introduces ZERO duplicate rows keyed on the full (strategy, account_id, run_generated_at) triple — 77 to 99 rows, 99 unique triples. The naive (strategy, account_id) key reports 44 'duplicates' and is misleading: gld_pullback_1h legitimately holds 55 rows over 5 runs, so that key collapses runs and must not be used as row identity here. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not reopen #11662/#11664 (they stay closed — only the non-redundant subset is landed, which serves the batch decision's intent to unjam the queue rather than reversing it), does not re-run the compat matrix, does not touch config/accounts.yaml, and does not fix the class that jammed all twelve — pr-landing R13 forcing a same-push session-board claim on a file with no merge driver in .gitattributes, which is #11519 and still stuck. Filed as BL-20260910-TWELVE-COMPAT-LANDING-PRS-WERE-CLOSED-AS-SUPERSEDED-ON-A-ROW-COUNT-AND-TWO-CARRIED-THE-ONLY-ALPACA-LIVE-VERDICTS-FOR-TWO-REAL-MONEY-LEGS, which also records that the recovery window is not permanent: these rows were recoverable only because the closed branches still existed when this was checked, and a pruned branch would have made the loss silent and final.
